The part that makes this a PMS answer rather than a media buyer's is the second half — you raise it with the client rather than quietly burning another cycle. Worth ruling out tracking first, but that's a day's work, not the conclusion.

questions.prompt: You inherit an account with one 40-day-old winner, no new angles tested this quarter, and spend stuck at $300/day. Which pillar do you work first, and why?
options: Scaling Winners — push the existing winner harder before anything else
Creative Diversity — produce more formats of the current winner
Angle Testing — without new angles there's nothing to diversify into or scale next
All three at once, to move faster
questions.explain: The winner is 40 days old and the spend is capped, which means it's near the end of its pocket. More formats of a tiring angle buys very little, and scaling something already saturating is how you burn it. Angle testing is what refills the other two pillars. "All three at once" is how you learn nothing from any of them.

questions.prompt: Walk the diagnostic ladder for a stuck account in the correct order:
options: Play 1: more/better ads → Play 2: better funnel for cold → Play 3: new platform
Play 1: new platform → Play 2: better funnel → Play 3: more ads
Play 1: raise budgets → Play 2: more ads → Play 3: new funnel
Play 1: better funnel → Play 2: more ads → Play 3: new platform
questions.explain: Strict order: creative diversity first (most accounts never finish it), then a better funnel for cold, then — rarely — a new platform.

questions.prompt: Surface metrics look fine, but lead quality has slid for months and the sales team is complaining. Which pattern?
options: The ceiling account
The slow-rot account
The over-reliant account
The saturation account
questions.explain: Slow-rot: healthy surface metrics, quietly degrading quality — usually a data/pixel problem.

questions.prompt: You changed the optimization event 4 days ago and numbers look worse. Do you revert?
options: No — Meta takes ~14 days to recalibrate after a pixel change; reverting at day 4 tells you nothing
Yes, revert immediately
Yes, and change a few other things too
Double the budget to speed it up
questions.explain: The 14-day rule. Hold pixel/optimization changes ~14 days before judging.

questions.prompt: A single book-a-call funnel has hit a frequency ceiling and won't scale. Best fix?
options: Raise the budget on the existing funnel
Run multiple funnels at different audience stages, each with its own optimization event
Narrow the audience targeting
Lower the bid cap
questions.explain: Different funnels (TOF lead magnet, MOF VSL, BOF retargeting) open pockets a single funnel can't reach.

questions.prompt: You're optimizing for Submit Application but only 1–3 events show in the last 7 days. First move?
options: Launch 20 fresh creatives
Confirm the optimization event is actually firing reliably (CAPI / automation) before changing anything
Raise the budget to force conversions
Switch to a new CAPI source today
questions.explain: Starved pixel — audit the firing mechanism first; don't touch creative or budget yet.

questions.prompt: Why exclude past purchasers and booked calls even on Advantage+ broad?
options: Because they cost more to reach
They're guardrails — they stop Meta recycling your existing pipeline instead of finding new people
Because Meta requires it
Because it lowers CPM
questions.explain: Exclusions are guardrails for prospecting, not targeting inputs.

questions.prompt: An info/high-ticket test campaign is outperforming your scaled CBO. Should you migrate its post-IDs into the CBO?
options: No — for info/high-ticket, scale in place; moving it makes Meta re-find a pocket and spikes call-cost volatility
Yes — always consolidate winners into a CBO
Yes — CBO is always cheaper
Delete the test and rebuild in the CBO
questions.explain: Scale in place for info/high-ticket. Post-ID-into-CBO suits high-volume e-com/low-ticket.

questions.prompt: A $13 CPM appears on a campaign meant to reach $150K+ earners. How do you read it?
options: A warning — you've drifted into a cheap, low-quality placement/pocket that won't convert
A win — scale it hard
Neutral — CPM means nothing
Proof the pixel is broken
questions.explain: Suspiciously low CPM on a high-value campaign = cheap traffic that won't convert. Investigate.

questions.prompt: An ad has a 2% CTR, 35% hook rate, and gorgeous thumb-stop — but zero sales. Do?
options: Scale it — sales will come
Kill it — engagement isn't the right attention; the wrong people clicking is worse than no one
Keep it at low budget for social proof
Lower the budget and wait a month
questions.explain: Vanity-metrics trap — kill it.

questions.prompt: A $12K/mo book-a-call account is generating six Schedule events a week. What's the right optimisation decision?
options: Stay on Schedule — it's the furthest-along event, so it's always correct
Optimise for Purchase instead, to pull better-qualified buyers
Raise the budget until Schedule volume arrives
Step back to an earlier event with enough volume, then move up to Schedule once it clears the learning threshold
questions.explain: The rule has two halves and this question tests the second one: the furthest-along event you can get volume on. Six a week is well under what the algorithm needs. Raising budget on a starved event mostly buys expensive noise, and Purchase is even thinner than Schedule on a call funnel.

questions.prompt: Two clients onboard the same week: one sells a $9K consulting retainer closed on a call, the other a $67 course with an upsell. What's the funnel pairing?
options: Webinar for both — it works at either price point
VSL for the retainer, low-ticket for the course
Low-ticket for the retainer, VSL for the course
Lead-magnet for both, then segment later
questions.explain: Two things decide it: price point, and whether a human closes. High-ticket and call-based is VSL. Sub-$100 self-serve closes in the funnel, so low-ticket. Lead-magnet-for-everything is the answer that avoids making the decision, and it costs you conversion on both.

questions.prompt: A prospect knows solutions exist and is comparing a few options before buying. Which stage?
options: Problem-aware
Solution-aware
Unaware
Most-aware / product-aware
questions.explain: Solution-aware → VSL / webinar / application territory.

questions.prompt: When and on what do you judge a lead magnet?
options: Day 14, on cost-per-lead
Day 60, on its pipeline contribution
Day 7, on direct ROAS
Day 30, on immediate revenue
questions.explain: Day 60, on pipeline contribution — not CPL/revenue at day 14.

questions.prompt: Same ad, same pixel, but a masculine vs. feminine page design. What happens to delivery?
options: Nothing — the page doesn't affect delivery
Meta serves them to different audiences — the page is a targeting signal
The feminine one gets rejected
Delivery is identical
questions.explain: The landing page is a targeting signal; Meta reads its copy and design.

questions.prompt: You test a new hook, new image, and new targeting all at once and a winner pops. What did you learn?
options: Nothing reliable — too many variables changed at once
That the image caused the win
That the targeting caused the win
Everything — it was a clean test
questions.explain: Isolate one variable. If you're testing everything, you're testing nothing.

questions.prompt: In a competitor's Ad Library you find one creative that's been running 47 days, and eleven launched in the past week. What do you conclude?
options: They're struggling — nobody launches eleven ads in a week if things are working
The eleven new ones are where the spend is going, so that's what to study
The 47-day ad is almost certainly their control — study that one before anything else
Nothing reliable. The Ad Library doesn't show spend
questions.explain: Longevity is the only free proxy for performance you get — nobody keeps paying to run a loser for 47 days. The eleven new ones are tests, and most will be dead in a fortnight. It's true that the library doesn't show spend, which makes that the tempting answer, but it doesn't make the library uninformative.

questions.prompt: Select all of the following that are LEADING indicators (move within 1–3 days).
options: CPM
Link CTR
CPC
Hook rate (3-sec views)
Cost per call
ROAS
questions.explain: Leading: CPM, CTR, CPC, hook rate, scroll-stop. Lagging: cost per call, ROAS, close rate.

questions.prompt: You launched 4 ads yesterday; day-1 CPC is 2–3× your normal. Wait for full 3× KPI spend, or pull?
options: Pull — when leading indicators are badly off on day one, you don't need to wait for full 3× KPI
Wait the full 3× KPI no matter what
Double the budget to gather data faster
Switch the optimization event immediately
questions.explain: Obvious day-one losers (CPC 2–3× normal) get cut early; the 3× rule is for ambiguous cases.

questions.prompt: You run five text-image ads where the only thing that changes is the callout persona ("Are you a home-service owner?", "…a fractional CFO?"). Which pillar/play is that?
options: Pillar 3 — scaling winners
Pillar 1 — creative diversity (the callout strategy lives here)
It's not a valid test
Audience targeting
questions.explain: Callouts are the fastest version of Pillar 1 — same offer/funnel, the callout is the only variable, finding new pockets.

questions.prompt: When writing a headline, which approach attracts better-converting buyers?
options: Call out the identity you want in the buyer ("Dallas executives")
Call out the guarantee to defuse objections ("or you don't pay")
Whatever wording gets the most clicks
Always lead with the lowest price
questions.explain: Identity callouts attract people already half-sold it's for them; guarantee/objection headlines attract skeptics who convert poorly.

questions.prompt: A "cold" Advantage+ broad campaign is showing 3–5x frequency over 30 days. Do you panic?
options: No — Advantage+ does baked-in retargeting, so high frequency is normal; don't panic
Yes — pause it immediately
Yes — exclude all audiences right away
Switch to tight manual interest stacks
questions.explain: Advantage+ bakes in retargeting, which drives 3–5x frequency even on "cold" campaigns. It's expected now.

questions.prompt: A client's page posts about fitness but the offer is business coaching, and Advantage+ keeps hammering the warm fitness audience. The fix?
options: Raise the budget on the main campaign
Switch the campaign to exact-match keywords
Run a low-budget cold-prospecting ad set excluding page engagers, ad engagers, video viewers, and site visitors
Delete the Facebook page
questions.explain: Page incongruence — exclude the warm engagers in a dedicated low-budget cold-prospecting ad set so Advantage+ finds new people (the Local Legend fix).

questions.prompt: In a lead-magnet funnel, how do the leads typically get converted?
options: Purchase happens in-funnel at checkout
They're sent straight to a webinar to buy
An outbound call from reps, supported by email nurture
A retargeting ad closes them automatically
questions.explain: The "call" in a lead-magnet funnel usually becomes outbound — reps call the leads, backed by nurture.

questions.prompt: Which headline targets a PROBLEM-aware prospect (knows the problem, not that solutions exist)?
options: "See why agents are switching from [Competitor] to our system"
"The real reason your listings keep going stale (and it's not your photos)"
"You've watched the demo — 20% off this week only"
"Book your strategy call — only 3 slots left"
questions.explain: Problem-aware headlines agitate the problem/curiosity without naming a solution. The others are solution-aware or most-aware.

questions.prompt: When you've found the weakest step in a funnel, which are the three levers you can pull (one at a time)?
options: Messaging (headline/copy)
Design (layout, colors, fonts)
Page structure (testimonials, step order, opt-in placement)
Bid strategy
Audience size
questions.explain: Messaging, design, and page structure — test one at a time. Fixing one weak step can halve cost-per-call without touching the ads.

questions.prompt: Your 7-day numbers look great but the 30-day is flat. What do you do?
options: You don't have a decision yet — investigate; recent vs. baseline disagree, especially on long high-ticket cycles
Cut everything immediately
Scale hard on the strength of the 7-day
Ignore the 30-day entirely
questions.explain: When the windows disagree you have a question, not a decision — high-ticket sales cycles are longer than you think.

questions.prompt: Your Schedule event is too low-volume for Meta to optimize on. Best move?
options: Step one event up the funnel (optimize a higher-volume qualified event) or run parallel optimization
Just raise the budget and wait
Switch all the creative
Do nothing — volume doesn't matter
questions.explain: Move one step up the funnel to a higher-volume but still-qualified event, or run parallel optimization events to feed the pixel.

questions.prompt: Select the conditions under which you'd cut an ad set BEFORE it reaches 3× KPI spend.
options: Day-1 click cost is 2–3× your normal
A diversity-play static has an absurd CPC
The ad has fewer than 100 likes
It hasn't hit 50 conversions yet
questions.explain: Cut early when leading indicators are obviously bad (CPC 2–3× normal) or a static's CPC is absurd. Likes and a 50-conversion count aren't kill signals.

questions.prompt: You want to test a new audience on a winning campaign. What do you do?
options: Duplicate the ad set (or launch a new one) — never modify a live, working ad set
Edit the live ad set directly to save time
Delete the ad set and rebuild it
Pause the whole campaign first
questions.explain: Never modify a live ad set — adding into it muddies data, steals delivery, and resets learning. Duplicate instead.

questions.prompt: A book-a-call client's calendar is nearly full for the week. What do you do with spend?
options: Scale hard regardless
Reduce spend — don't pay to book an already-full calendar
Pause all ads for the rest of the week
Switch the optimization event
questions.explain: Pace spend to availability: few open slots → ease off; lots of openings → room to scale.

questions.prompt: A winning ad set has plateaued around $350/day. What's the AdClass scaling move?
options: Duplicate it with the same post-ID into a new ad set to find a fresh pocket
Force 3× more budget through the same ad set
Kill it — it's clearly fatigued
Cut its budget in half
questions.explain: Pocket theory: duplicate the winner into a parallel ad set (same post-ID) — it often finds a new pocket that scales independently. Degrading on added budget can mean the pocket is tapped, not that the ad is dead.

questions.prompt: In 2026, is the browser-side pixel alone enough for clean conversion data?
options: No — CAPI (server-side) must be set up, with events deduplicated against the browser pixel
Yes — the browser pixel is plenty
Only for e-commerce accounts
Only when Hyros is down
questions.explain: CAPI is a non-negotiable in 2026 — server-side events give cleaner signal; dedupe them against the browser pixel so Meta doesn't double-count.

questions.prompt: You're handed two live accounts and told nothing. After diagnosing one as failing and one as ready to scale, what do you deliver?
options: The same generic checklist for both
Only the failing account matters
A turnaround plan (diagnosis → sequence → timeline) for the failing one, and a scale plan (where/how to add spend, expected volatility) for the other
Wait for someone to tell you which is which
questions.explain: Two accounts, two different jobs. The diagnosis determines which document you're writing — and neither is a checklist.

questions.prompt: On a client call you're asked about a scary-looking one-day dip. Best response?
options: Explain what it is, whether it's normal (a single-day read vs the 7/14/30 trend), and the plan — calm and specific
Panic and promise to fix it today
Say you'll have to check, and end the call
Blame Meta
questions.explain: Context, then plan, delivered calmly. Promising a same-day fix for a single-day read commits you to something that probably didn't need fixing.

questions.prompt: A client asks, 'Meta shows 40 leads but our CRM shows 22 — which is real?' Best answer?
options: The CRM is broken
Meta is lying
Ignore both and use GA4
Both are 'real' but measure different things — Meta counts click/view attribution in its window; the CRM is booked truth. For revenue decisions we lead with the CRM / Hyros number.
questions.explain: The gap isn't a fault, it's two different definitions. Naming which one you make decisions on — and why — is what stops this becoming a monthly argument.

questions.tag: Exam · Why fire CAPI from the CRM
questions.prompt: Why fire conversion events from the CRM via CAPI instead of relying on the browser pixel?
options: It's cheaper
The CRM knows the real qualified/booked event and sends it server-side — bypassing browser / iOS / ad-block gaps and feeding Meta cleaner signal
Meta requires it on all accounts
It removes the need for any pixel
questions.explain: Server-side from the CRM means the event Meta optimizes toward is the one that actually matters commercially, and it survives the browser-side gaps. It supplements the pixel rather than replacing it.

questions.prompt: A client asks why you want to add a second funnel instead of 'just spending more' on the one that works. Best framing?
options: More funnels are always better
The current funnel is broken

A single funnel taps one finite pocket — frequency and CPMs climb to a ceiling. New funnels at different awareness stages open new pockets, each with its own optimization event, so spend can grow profitably.
We actually need to lower the budget
questions.explain: The honest version: the existing funnel isn't broken, it's finite. A second funnel at a different awareness stage is how the spend ceiling moves. Note that neither 'more is better' nor 'it's broken' is true here.

questions.prompt: Which audit recommendation is 'client-ready'?
options: 'The account could be doing better.'
'TOF CTR is 0.5% and the hero angle is fatiguing — we're testing 3 new hooks this week; expect cost-per-lead to settle over ~2 weeks.'
'Creative needs work.'
'Let's just raise the budget.'
questions.explain: Client-ready means the observation, the action, and the expectation — all specific enough to be checked against later.

questions.tag: Exam · A question you can't answer
questions.prompt: In the audit role-play, the 'client' asks something you don't know. Best response?
options: Make up a confident-sounding answer
Deflect and change the subject
